chunk_findings.detail: The removed `row["requested_by"] != canon.agent` guard is not replaced by the intended “same wave/coordinator or successor lane” restriction. Since `canon.digest()` no longer includes `agent`, the remaining identity check is just the verb plus the action/state digest. Input: lane A in wave W1 has an ANSWERED approval `ask_id=A1` for gate-skip on item I with outcome O. Lane B in unrelated wave W2 runs the same gate-skip on the same I/O and supplies `A1`. `row["verb"] == canon.verb` and the agent-free digest now match, and the owner check is gone, so B spends A1. That is wrong because B is not a successor lane of A’s wave/coordinator; the change authorizes any agent anywhere in the system that can reproduce the same action, not just a successor in the intended scope.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/consume.py:70

chunk_findings.detail: The “widened act” assertion creates `other` as an approval for `_canon(item="fix-OTHER")` and then calls `C.operator_gate(successor, cfg, _canon(agent="successor", item="fix-OTHER"), approval_id=other.id, now=T0 + 1)` and asserts it fails. But that call is an exact match for `other.id` under the rule this test is establishing: the approval belongs to the action, not the agent, and the successor is re-running the same item/state. The test should pass `filed.id` while requesting `item="fix-OTHER"` to show the old approval cannot be reused for a widened action. As written, the regression test fails on a correct implementation, or the implementation must incorrectly refuse a freshly granted, exact-match approval.

chunk_findings.detail: The test is renamed to assert the digest binds everything except the agent and the agent's reason, but the body never creates a Canon differing only in `reason` and never asserts those digests are equal. chunk_findings.detail: The digest schema drops `agent` but leaves the record version at `"v": 1` and provides no migration or recomputation for already-stored approvals. An unspent approval row created before this change has `row["digest"]` computed from the old record that included `agent`; after deploy, a successor re-running the exact action gets a new `canon.digest()` without `agent`, so the stored digest no longer matches and the spend is rejected. Input: pre-change lane A gets an ANSWERED approval for item I and dies before spending; after deploy, successor lane B re-runs the same verb/item/target/args/state, but `judge` compares the old stored digest to B's new agent-free digest and refuses the claim. This leaves the exact unspent approvals the fix is meant to rescue still stranded.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test asserts that `thief` (with no established successor-lane/same-wave relationship) can spend an approval requested by `asker`, and the matching `gate_skip`/`mcp` tests do the same for `mallory`.
